title: Autotune sandbox A/B test for dynamic prefetch + mini-batch policies
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Goal: Validate an automated recommender that proposes per-model 'mini-batch' sizes and KV-prefetch thresholds and verify end-to-end safety (latency SLOs and output quality) under real traffic. We will run a two-arm randomized A/B where control uses current stable policies and treatment uses the recommender + safe-apply gate. Key questions: 1) Can the recommender reduce per-token cost >= 8% without >2% tail latency regressions? 2) Does prefix/KV prefetching increase cache hit-rate for long-tail sessions? 3) Are our rollback gates sensitive and fast enough to prevent customer-facing SLO violations?
success_criteria: Treatment shows >=8% cost reduction per-request (median tokens cost) with p<0.05 on bootstrapped mean; 95th percentile latency delta <= +2% and no significant increase in user-level error rate; automated rollback triggers correctly within 5 minutes when safety thresholds exceeded.
experiment_design:
- Traffic split: 20% treatment / 80% control across 10% sampled production traffic (to limit blast radius).
- Cohorts: BY model family (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder), by sequence-length bucket (short<64, mid 64-512, long>512), by customer tier (free/paid).
- Duration: minimum 7 days or until reach statistical power (80%) for cost metric.
- Instrumentation: per-request token cost, raw inference time (compute-only), end-to-end latency, tail latencies (p90,p95,p99), KV cache hit rate, model output quality signal (BLEU for structured tasks or surrogate scoring), error rates, and rollback events.
- Safety gates: immediate rollback if p95 latency increases >3% relative to control for two consecutive 5-minute windows OR error rate increases >0.5 percentage points in a 10-minute window.
- Analysis plan: use bootstrapped confidence intervals for cost; hierarchical modeling to control for model-family and customer-tier variance; run online A/B metrics with sequential testing correction (alpha spending) to allow early stopping while controlling false positives.
instrumentation_notes: Added tags to request logs: experiment_id=ENG-53210, cohort, seed_version, applied_policy_id. KV cache metrics emitted per-host and per-model (hits, misses, bytes_prefetched).: Added light-weight quality hooks to sample 1% of responses for offline eval jobs. Event schema changes submitted in PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/1198.
runbook:
- How to start: flip feature-flag eng.autotune.abtest.53210 rollout in Console -> feature-flags -> enable on staging and 10% prod.
- How to monitor: Dashboard link (Grafana) -> Experiment/ENG-53210. Observe cost_delta, p95_latency_delta, kv_hit_rate.
- How to rollback: Use Console -> Rollouts -> Abort experiment or set eng.autotune.abtest.53210=false. For emergency, run scripts/ops/safe_rollback.sh to revert runtime policy state across pods.
- Post-mortem steps: collect traces for affected requests, correlate with model-version churn and HW topology.

notes_and_tradeoffs:
- Tradeoff: heavier prefetch increases KV traffic and memory pressure on GPU nodes; limited to per-model soft cap for first rollout.
- Decision: start conservative with prefetch budget 0.75x predicted while we collect hit-rate signals.
- Tradeoff: minibatch increases per-request latency variance; we prefer slightly higher median throughput with strict p95 constraints.
- If cost wins are small (<6%) we'll iterate on recommender features (sequence-length-aware batching, dynamic burst windows) before larger rollout.
